svg.text: One fixed Seahorse Valley center, six spans, and a tighter question than a single glamour zoom: how does the slow-escape mix change as the boundary folds inward?
Each frame uses the same smooth-escape palette. The charts below track mean smooth escape and the share of escaped pixels still dragging above 65% of the iteration budget.
Average dwell among escaped pixels. This is the broad texture meter.
zoom level on a fixed Seahorse Valley center
higher means more pixels stay near the boundary longer
Escaped pixels still above 65% of the iteration budget. This catches the slow tail directly.
zoom level on a fixed Seahorse Valley center
fraction of escaped pixels in the slow tail
The point is not that zooming always makes the same metric rise. The point is that the slow-escape mix changes shape with scale, so a good zoom sequence is more than six prettier posters.
